headline: Red Sox and Patriots both drop games in ugly fashion
morning_brew: That four to six loss to the Angels was a gut punch, especially seeing the bats stay cold in the freezer until the ninth. Jake Bennett had a rough go on the mound, giving up six runs in five and a third innings, which put us in a hole deeper than the construction on the Pike. It is hard to watch the team lose ground while the Duck Boat fund is currently frozen pending investigation, but that is the reality of the stretch run. We need the starting rotation to be steadier if we want to hold onto our spot, or I might need to start a dossier on the pitching staff similar to the one neighbor Rick has on the local mailman.

Switching over to the gridiron, the Patriots suffered a tough ten to thirteen loss to the Seahawks. Drake Maye threw for one hundred seventy-eight yards and a touchdown, but those three interceptions were absolute backbreakers in a defensive slog where every possession was precious. It is a miserable start to the season, and it is infuriating to see us cough one up in such a winnable battle. We have a lot of season left to right the ship, but nobody in the Hub enjoys waking up on the wrong side of the loss column.

Looking ahead, we have a series against the Royals starting Thursday at Fenway. The boys need to wash off the taste of yesterday and get back to playing the kind of baseball that actually put us in the postseason conversation. I am hoping for a cleaner game all around, and maybe the bats can find some actual rhythm against Kansas City. It is a long road through September, so let us see if we can turn this mess around before I lose my mind.
